record_type_quote: This exercise reproduces and assesses the historical time-series on the top shares of the wealth distribution for the United States presented by Thomas Piketty in Capital in the Twenty-First Century.

targets.title: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
targets.evidence_quote: The raw numbers presented in Figure 1 were the “bedrock” employed by Piketty to produce the chart he published as Figure 10.5 and which I reproduce here as Figure 2 [Piketty 2014a: 348, 2014b: 1].
targets.outcome_computational_quote: For 1980 Piketty reported that he averaged the 1983 figure from Wolff [1994] with the 1989 Federal Reserve figure from Kennickell [2009]. Had he done that, the number would be 67.7, but he reported 67.2 (which is the 1989 figure unaveraged).
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: For 1870 Piketty reports Soltow’s number taken from Lindert, 71 percent, but without applying the 1.2 multiplier that he used on the top one-percent wealth share, which consistency suggests he should have done. Had he done so, his 1870 figure would be 85.2 percent of the wealth in the hands of the top 10 percent. But that figure implies there was a fall in the wealth share between 1870 and 1910.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Reconstruction yields substantive discrepancies in reported shares; alternative constructions of the same source estimates qualify the historical trend.

targets.title: Inequality in the Long Run
targets.evidence_quote: At least in the issue of Science for May 23, 2014 he has a coauthored review with Emmanuel Saez which presents his data for the top ten percent but does not present the companion series for the top one percent [Piketty and Saez 2014: Figure 2, 839]. I replicate the figure from Science here as Figure 4. It reproduced the data in Figure 10.6 from Piketty’s book except it drops the point for 1810, but it now inexplicably adds a point for 1890 that isn't in the book’s version.

reasoning: Reconstructs published series from the original source estimates and checks alternative manipulations. The Science figure is explicitly reconstructed and its top-decile data examined, so it is a separate target; source studies and technical appendices are not counted as separate originals. Full text acquired is the author’s December 2015 draft, not the final 2017 version; title, author, focus, and abstract establish a version of this work, but version differences remain an uncertainty.
